76939.subject: 🐉 Claude Mythos scares China's president
76939.body:
----------
######                  [Collaborate with us](https://utm.genai.works/r/he2t9cz)


--------------------
View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/8776fa6e-e2d0-4aec-9648-1bed6de3a659/GenAI_Daily_Banner.jpg?t=1778687445)
Caption: 


----------

----------
**Welcome back!** Beijing is calling Anthropic's most dangerous model a possible weapon seven weeks before Xi lands in America, and the White House finished its AI rulebook and put four labs in a room today. Visa dropped $2.4 billion on a company that reads your keystrokes, and Dario Amodei told colleagues he's worried his new hires only came for the paycheck.

**In today's Generative AI Newsletter:**

* **China:** What does Beijing want from Anthropic?

* **White House:** What can the government do to a model before it ships?

* **Visa:** What is it buying for $2.4 billion?

* **Anthropic:** Why is Dario unhappy with his own hires?


----------



----------
## China issues a warning about Mythos

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/b5d1e61f-13e4-4643-8a44-7772b42a3e30/ChatGPT_Image_Aug_4__2026__11_51_24_AM.png?t=1785833513)
Caption: 

Beijing thinks Claude Mythos could be turned on it, and it picked a loaded moment to say so. Xi visits the US on [September 24](https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/2026/08/04/tech/china-mythos-trump-xi/), with AI talks expected before the two leaders meet.

Officials see models like Mythos as a possible offensive weapon, and they want to know why Anthropic denies China access for ordinary use while American companies get it.

Beijing isn't preparing anything yet. It's drawing up responses in case Washington moves first, and the options include sanctions or putting American AI companies on a restricted-entity list.

Wu Xinbo, who runs Fudan University's Center for American Studies, put the fear plainly. US AI companies collect customer data and can hand it to the American government or military.

Anthropic is an awkward target. Dario Amodei has pushed Washington to keep chips out of China and accused Alibaba's Qwen team of training on Claude's outputs. 

The company blocked Chinese-controlled firms last year and doesn't operate in China at all, so sanctions would sting reputationally more than financially.

Washington isn't easy on Anthropic either. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick made it get licenses in June before serving Mythos 5 and Fable 5 to any foreign entity, and Anthropic switched the models off until it worked something out.

Looks like Anthropic got problems with the two world leaders. Let’s keep an eye on how it’s going to play out, especially after the new regulations USA wants to introduce.  


----------









----------
